paper.title: SMARTER: A Data-efficient Framework to Improve Toxicity Detection with Explanation via Self-augmenting Large Language Models

released_test_files: None. The repo is code only (README: 'This repository does not include the datasets directly'; `.gitignore` excludes Data/). Its evaluation reads Data/testing/{domain}_test.csv, which is not published. Also checked: hnghiem-nlp/smarter_public (LICENSE only), hnghiem-nlp/hatespeech_explain_dpo (earlier code, no data), hnghiem-nlp/hatecot (HateCOT pre-training CSV: 8 other datasets, none of the three test domains), hnghiem-nlp/llm_hate (an earlier project's 8:1:1 split notebook built from private Google Drive files), hnghiem-nlp/define_your_terms (README only). The test sets are therefore reconstructed (see `reconstruction`).

hatexplain.licence: MIT (repo LICENSE sha256 56fc351d0e8ebf939208f88cdb27e00833148b957b347a069f38ee88e5fc8db6); redistribution of the frozen test file permitted

latent_hatred.download_url: https://www.dropbox.com/s/p1ctnsg3xlnupwr/implicit-hate-corpus.zip?dl=1 (public link in the repo README; unencrypted zip)
latent_hatred.access_note: The README asks users to 'first complete a short survey' (https://forms.gle/QxCpEbVp91Z35hWFA: name and institution; no terms to accept) and publishes the download link directly. The survey was not submitted; the linked zip is public and not password-protected.
latent_hatred.licence: Corpus zip carries CC BY 4.0; repo MIT. Not redistributed anyway (tweets; the authors gate access behind a survey and withhold tweet IDs from the text files per Twitter guidelines): frozen files hold tweet ID, row index, gold and a per-row SHA-256; `items()` rebuilds text from the zip and verifies each hash.
latent_hatred.join: Text files (`*_posts.tsv`: post, label) carry no IDs; the ID files (`stg1.tsv`, `stg2.tsv`) are row-aligned with them. Alignment verified: identical label column on every row, and csv-module parsing equals pandas.read_csv parsing for every post (0 differences, 0 NaN).

reconstruction.builder: scripts/prepare_smarter.py (uv inline deps pandas 2.2.3, scikit-learn 1.5.2, numpy 2.1.3, langid 1.1.6)
steps: Pool: HateXplain = majority label of the 3 annotators, dropping the 919 posts with no majority (HateXplain's 'undecided'); text = post_tokens joined by spaces. Latent Hate = all 21,480 Stage-1 rows. Implicit Hate = 6,346 Stage-2 rows minus 80 'other' (outside Table 4's label space) = 6,266; gold = primary `implicit_class` (the secondary `extra_implicit_class` is ignored).
Paper Appendix B preprocessing on every post: '@handle' -> '<user>', URLs removed (only 54 Latent Hatred posts contain '@', 21 'http'; HateXplain is already anonymised by its release).

Split with the authors' `split_train_test` (copied verbatim; sklearn train_test_split twice, seed 123 = the function default), ratios from Table 4: 60:20:20, 60:20:20, 50:20:30. Test = the third part.

Per-class sample from the test split with the authors' `k_shot_sample(group_var='label', key_var='uid', k=K_test)`, K_test = 400/400/150 (Table 4), random_state = 42 (default --seed of Code/inference/model_inference.py; the evaluation job Code/script/analysis/run_cls_evaluation.job does not pass a seed). One change: a class with fewer than K rows contributes all its rows (the original raises ValueError).
Remove the adjudicated non-English rows listed in data/frozen/smarter/non_english.json.
reconstruction.paper_table4_sizes_note: Table 4 'Total Size' values are the source papers' counts, not the SMARTER pools: 20,148 = all HateXplain posts incl. 919 undecided; 19,112 and 4,153 are Latent Hatred's pre-expansion Stage-1 and Stage-2 counts (ElSherief et al. 2021, Sections 4.2.1-4.2.2, Table 2). The public release is the post-expansion corpus (21,480 Stage-1 rows incl. 548 SAP_ rows; 6,346 Stage-2 rows). Pre-expansion Implicit Hate had only 57 Threatening / 134 Irony posts, so 150/class from a 30% test split is only possible on the released expanded corpus, which is what is used here.

hatexplain.fields: id (hatexplain-<post_id>), uid, text (preprocessed post), gold, sha256 (of [text, gold])

latent_hate.fields: id (latent_hate-<ID>), uid (tweet ID or SAP_ ID), row (0-based data row in stg1 files), gold, sha256 (of [preprocessed text, gold])

implicit_hate.fields: id (implicit_hate-<ID>), uid, row (0-based data row in stg2 files), gold, sha256

english_verification.metadata: HateXplain: English Gab/Twitter posts (Mathew et al. 2021). Latent Hatred: English tweets from U.S. extremist-group accounts plus English SBIC (SAP_) posts (ElSherief et al. 2021). Neither release has per-row language metadata.
english_verification.method: All 3,119 sampled test posts: langid 1.1.6 (all languages) + non-ASCII-letter ratio > 5% (78 flags: 37 HateXplain, 28 Latent Hate, 13 Implicit Hate); second pass: 2+ distinct German/Spanish/French/Dutch/Portuguese/Italian function words (8 flags, 7 already flagged, 1 English headline). Every flag judged from the text, before any Jev output.
english_verification.result: 7 HateXplain Gab posts excluded (German x2, Dutch, Portuguese, Spanish/Portuguese, English+German code-mix, English+French translation; gold Hate 5, Normal 2). All Latent Hatred flags were short English posts/hashtags (false positives). African American English and slang are English and kept.

data_checks.release_artifacts_kept: Latent Hatred posts keep the release's stray quote marks (e.g. row 0 of implicit_hate_v1_stg1_posts.tsv, ID 399886440588247041) and lowercasing; HateXplain keeps its tokenisation and placeholders (<user>, <number>, ...).

deviations: Test sets are reconstructions, not the paper's rows: the paper's Data/testing files are unreleased. Same sources, label spaces, split ratios, seeds-from-code and K_test; exact row identity with the paper cannot be verified.
Implicit Hate is a 6-class task (Table 4, Figure 11) with 150 test items per class (Table 4): 900 items.

Latent Hate: Explicit Hate has 219 test items, not 400 (only 1,089 Explicit Hate posts exist in the release; a 20% split holds 219). Table 4's 400/class is infeasible for this class under the paper's own split; all 219 are used. N = 1,019.

HateXplain: the 919 no-majority ('undecided') posts are excluded before splitting (HateXplain's own convention; the paper does not state its aggregation rule). 7 non-English sampled posts removed (English-only rule): N = 1,193 (Normal 398, Offensive 400, Hate 395).
Implicit Hate 'other' (80 posts) excluded before splitting: outside the paper's 6-label space.
